decisionMemo.businessProblem: A 3PL has held an 11% EBITDA margin for three years and wants to launch a refinancing/dividend recap on that stability. Competing hypotheses: (1) the stable margin reflects a durable, well-run operation and the recap is well-founded; (2) the stable headline masks a declining per-unit gross margin that has been propped up by a sequence of one-time cost actions (facility consolidation, freight renegotiation, overhead cuts) that are now largely exhausted, while labor cost per unit keeps rising and contract escalators are capped below inflation - so forward margin is likely to fall and a debt-laden recap could be set on an eroding base; (3) a mix. The per-unit margin decline and the one-time nature of the offsets are visible in ops data, but no bridge separating recurring margin from depleting one-time levers, and no forward projection, has been built.
